o.text: Borrowed from Arabic قَانُون (qānūn), ultimately from Ancient Greek κανών (kanṓn).
From Proto-Turkic *KApur. Cognate with Turkmen gapyrga, Crimean Tatar qaburğa, Bashkir ҡабырға (qabırğa).
Present participle compound of gözə (“eye”, dative) + çarp- (“to strike”)
From Proto-Common Turkic *kaška-lak, from Proto-Common Turkic *kaška (“bald/white spot on the forehead”), thus equivalent to qaşqa + -laq.
Borrowed from Classical Persian کاهریز (compare modern Persian کاریز).
